sections.section_title: From Screening Abnormality to Suspicion of MODY: Case Presentation and Key Clues
sections.description: Introduces the patient’s presentation and highlights clinical signals that raise suspicion for HNF1A-MODY rather than type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Establishes the clinical logic from first encounter to a targeted diagnostic pathway.
subtopics: Demographics and family pedigree: multigenerational early-onset diabetes suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical phenotype at diagnosis: marked hyperglycaemia (HbA1c 10.2%), post-OGTT hyperglycaemia, glycosuria without ketoacidosis
Physical examination and metabolic profile: BMI 24.6 kg/m2, no acanthosis; triglycerides and HDL features that can confound with T2D
Glycosuria as a clue: reduced renal glucose threshold typical of HNF1A deficiency
Early symptoms (polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss) that overlap with T1D/T2D and challenge initial classification
Red flags for MODY in young-onset diabetes and common pitfalls leading to misclassification

sections.section_title: Building the Differential and Executing the Workup
sections.description: Details the stepwise differential diagnosis of diabetes in a young adult and the targeted investigations that refine pretest probability for MODY. Explains how each test result shifted diagnostic likelihood in this case.
subtopics: Differential diagnosis: type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, LADA, MODY subtypes, and secondary diabetes
Islet autoantibodies (GADA, IA-2A, ZnT8): interpretation, timing, and caveats (occasional seropositivity in MODY)
C-peptide assessment strategies: fasting vs stimulated; glucagon stimulation thresholds and nuances (patient: 0.39 to 0.83 nmol/L—moderately preserved yet insufficient secretion)
OGTT and postprandial dysglycaemia as supportive evidence for MODY
Sudomotor testing: what reduced electrochemical skin conductance means and its limitations in early disease
Clinical prediction tools (Exeter MODY calculator): use, thresholds, and limitations in non-White populations (patient probability ≈62%)
Indications to proceed to genetic testing; choosing an NGS panel and integrating clinical-biochemical context

sections.section_title: HNF1A-MODY: Molecular Basis, Pathophysiology, and Variant Interpretation
sections.description: Explains the biology of HNF1A, how its dysfunction causes the observed phenotype, and how the novel variant in this case was classified using modern genomics frameworks. Connects molecular findings to clinical expression and family counseling.
subtopics: HNF1A gene and protein: location, domains (dimerization, DNA-binding, transactivation), and tissue expression (pancreas, liver, kidney)
Pathophysiology: progressive β-cell dysfunction via impaired insulin/GLUT2 expression and pyruvate kinase activity; reduced renal glucose threshold via downregulated SGLT2
Clinical signature of HNF1A-MODY: early-onset nonautoimmune diabetes, glycosuria, high sensitivity to insulin secretagogues, overlap with T1D/T2D later in disease
Genetic testing workflow: NGS panel selection, variant curation, and ACMG criteria (population data, segregation, in silico prediction, domain/function evidence)
Case variant p.N270S (c.809A>G): DNA-binding domain location; absence from ClinVar/VarSome; AlphaMissense score; familial segregation supporting likely pathogenic/pathogenic classification
Implications for relatives: cascade testing, penetrance expectations, variable expressivity, and genetic counseling

sections.section_title: Precision Therapy in HNF1A-MODY: From Initial Control to Long-term Management
sections.description: Outlines therapeutic principles tailored to HNF1A-MODY, from acute glycaemic control to individualized maintenance therapy. Compares drug classes, summarizes evidence, and provides rationale for the regimen used in the case.
subtopics: Initial management of marked hyperglycaemia: indications for temporary basal insulin and criteria for de-escalation after stabilization
Sulfonylureas as traditional first-line in HNF1A-MODY: low-dose strategy, efficacy, and hypoglycaemia risk

GLP-1 receptor agonists vs sulfonylureas: randomized crossover data (liraglutide vs glimepiride), glycaemic efficacy, weight effects, and hypoglycaemia profile; rationale for dulaglutide in this patient
Roles of metformin and DPP-4 inhibitors: adjuncts when insulin resistance or weight considerations coexist; tailoring to β-cell reserve
SGLT2 inhibitors in HNF1A-MODY: mechanistic concerns (baseline reduced SGLT2), risks of dehydration and ketoacidosis; when to avoid
Targets, monitoring, and lifestyle: HbA1c goals, SMBG/CGM use, complication screening, nutrition, and physical activity

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Follow-up, and Key Clinical Lessons
sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s course and consolidates practice-changing lessons on diagnosis, treatment, and systems-level considerations for MODY detection and care.
subtopics: Patient trajectory: HbA1c drop from 10.2% to 6.0% in 6 months; maintenance <6.5% after insulin withdrawal and GLP-1 RA/DPP-4 inhibitor plus metformin
Complication surveillance: absent microalbuminuria/retinopathy to date; interpreting early sudomotor abnormalities and follow-up planning
Impact of genetic confirmation: precision therapy, deprescribing insulin, patient education, and adherence
Cost-effectiveness and access: when genetic testing alters management; optimizing selection criteria to improve yield
Practical algorithm and red flags for clinicians: who to test, how to interpret results, and common diagnostic pitfalls in diverse populations
Future directions: expanding variant catalogs, improving prediction tools beyond European cohorts, and integrating genomics into routine diabetes care
